steps.name: Keen Famiglia Juror
steps.text: Tsk, tsk. The courtroom sure is lively today.

steps.name: Composed Famiglia Juror
steps.text: Today's trial will be open to the general public, and broadcasted live. Far too many people will be joining in on the fun.

steps.name: Keen Famiglia Juror
steps.text: Heh, this is the first time I've seen jurors representing so many different famiglie arrive in such an orderly fashion. This almost seems more like a press conference than a trial.

steps.name: Composed Famiglia Juror
steps.text: After all, the man on trial today is none other than Leontuzzo Bellone.

steps.name: Composed Famiglia Juror
steps.text: Signora Sicilia gave the order that 'the famiglie are not to interfere with the new city' but didn't elaborate on her plans beyond that. Everybody's scratching their heads.

steps.name: Composed Famiglia Juror
steps.text: Finally, the court representing Signora Sicilia's will is about to make its move, so of course it has everyone's undivided attention.

steps.name: Keen Famiglia Juror
steps.text: But, the woman adjudicating the trial is that Judge Lavinia, and everybody knows she's tied up with the Bellones.

steps.name: Composed Famiglia Juror
steps.text: There's no Bellones anymore, they're stricken from the books. What kind of connections could she have?

steps.name: Composed Famiglia Juror
steps.text: If you ask me, she's taking the initiative to convict Leontuzzo, exactly because she wants to show everybody she's done with the Bellones.

steps.name: Keen Famiglia Juror
steps.text: And besides, Signora Sicilia's made it pretty clear what she's up to here. She's gonna make an example of him.

steps.name: Keen Famiglia Juror
steps.text: She's playing her cards well.

steps.name: Composed Famiglia Juror
steps.text: Who knows.

steps.name: Composed Famiglia Juror
steps.text: Anyways, since Bernardo was the mastermind behind everything, his son's obviously involved. Today's trial should give us the closure we're looking for.

steps.name: Keen Famiglia Juror
steps.text: Fair enough.

steps.name: Composed Famiglia Juror
steps.text: Look, the judge is here.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Order in the court.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Presumably, many of you are perplexed about today's hearing.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: That is to be expected, because while you may know the man on trial today, you do not know the contents of the case.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I ask that you all remain patient.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I trust that nobody has forgotten that day, one week ago.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: So much happened. Minister Rubio's broadcast, and the ensuing chaos that engulfed the city.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Many people died during that turmoil, and many others had their lives turned upside-down.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Fortunately, it was all eventually smoothed over.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Many people know now that Bernardo Bellone, the man who instigated this chaos, lost his life to it as well.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Yet his objectives, as well as his motives, remain mysterious.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: During that incident, another man played an important role. He is none other than Bernardo Bellone's son, Leontuzzo Bellone.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Bring him forward.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Order, order.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: For some of you, this may be your first time seeing me. For others, you might've known me for a long time.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: But first, allow me to introduce myself. I am Leontuzzo Bellone, and I am just an ordinary civilian now.

steps.name: Juror
steps.text: Ordinary civilian? Aren't you the heir to Famiglia Bellone?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I was. But now, I do not belong to any famiglia.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I know you all have many questions, and I will answer them one by one. First and foremost, however, I must explain what my father did, and how it came to this.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: All of this most likely began with the death of Carracci, Ministero dei Lavori Pubblici.
Leontuzzo, standing at the center of the courtroom under the watchful eyes of the entire crowd, shows no signs of nerves at all.
He methodically lays out the backdrop to this entire incident, starting from the assassination.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: The other famiglie seem to have already received the news about the ownership of the new city.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I know. 'The famiglie are not to interfere with the new city.'

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: That she's willing to hold down the other famiglie is proof she wasn't lying when we talked.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: But as far as I know, she neither said who would manage the new nomadic city, nor did she explain her rationale.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: That's how Grey Hall has always worked.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Signora Sicilia doesn't need to explain everything. Her orders are absolute.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: But, we need her explanation.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Right now, everything about the new city is shrouded in uncertainty, and we owe the people an explanation.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: That's right, which also brings us to our first dilemma.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Everything happened so suddenly. Am I supposed to get up on stage and announce to everyone, 'hey, we're going to build a city without famiglie?'

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: That would only scare everyone away.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: If the only ones who end up there are you, me, Cellinia, and Rubio's followers, we've already failed at the very first step.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I'm guessing Signora Sicilia wants to see how we handle this.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Looks like you have something in mind.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I do.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I want you to arrest me, Lavinia.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Come again?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: My father's actions, no matter his motivations and intentions, put us in this mess.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Someone must be held accountable, in the eyes of the people.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Besides, I'm doing the same thing, aren't I?
The assassination of Carracci, the alliance with the Saluzzos, the assassination of Donna Rossati, and finally, the separation of the secondary core area.
Though some of these events were not secret, when people learned that Bernardo was the driving force behind them, a commotion still broke out in the courtroom.
Leontuzzo lays out his father's plan as objectively as possible using the information he has.
Finally, after an hour-long exposition, the story comes to an end.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I know that many of you are here on behalf of various famiglie, and I assume you've all heard a number of rumors.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: That one rumor is correct.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Everything was my father's doing, and the reason why he did it was––

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: 'For a Siracusa without famiglie.'

steps.name: Confused Government Observer
steps.text: How is it possible that the don of a famiglia would want to tear down the entire system?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Good question. Even I, his own son, was shocked when I found out.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: This idea took root in my father's heart decades ago. And it only just now bore fruit.

steps.name: Keen Famiglia Juror
steps.text: Leontuzzo, drop the act already. Your father's dead, but you're still here. That's why you're trying to clear your name with all this nonsense.

steps.name: Composed Famiglia Juror
steps.text: After all, we know exactly who the new city belongs to.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I can handle accusations from some famiglie associates or soldiers, if that makes you happy.

steps.name: Skeptical Civilian
steps.text: If he was the mastermind behind all this, then why did he end up dead?
Il Signore dei Lupi.
Leontuzzo almost blurts the words, but finally suppresses them within his heart.
Because, everything about that existence is utterly absurd.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: My father believed that if famiglie should not exist, then he should be eliminated too.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: So, after setting everything in motion, he chose to commit suicide.

steps.name: Irascible Famiglia Juror
steps.text: Pretty damned good joke there, kid!

steps.name: Irascible Famiglia Juror
steps.text: You're telling me he was such a selfless saint? He really did all this for the common Siracusan?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: The exact opposite, actually.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: My father was solipsistic, if anything. Everything he did was for the sake of the painting in his memory he called Siracusa.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Which is why he failed.

steps.name: Irascible Famiglia Juror
steps.text: Alright... I get it now.

steps.name: Irascible Famiglia Juror
steps.text: Hah, no wonder. That's why Bernardo's dead, and you're still alive.

steps.name: Irascible Famiglia Juror
steps.text: I dunno what kind of stunt you pulled, but you somehow stopped your papa, and then went to Signora Sicilia and took credit for it.

steps.name: Irascible Famiglia Juror
steps.text: That's how you got yourself the right to manage the new city. And now, you're up here spinning a magical tale for us, trying to win some sympathy for yourself.

steps.name: Irascible Famiglia Juror
steps.text: Isn't that right, you patricide?
Leontuzzo lets out a deep sigh, but in the end, looks away without refuting the accusation.
Deep down, he cannot deny it.

steps.name: Irascible Famiglia Juror
steps.text: Look at that, see the guilt on his face!

steps.name: Calm Civilian Juror
steps.text: I have a question.

steps.name: Calm Civilian Juror
steps.text: Even if we did believe all that garbage, Your Honor, what does it have to do with the trial?

steps.name: Calm Civilian Juror
steps.text: It's not like you want us passing judgment on a dead man and handing down a sentence for his crimes?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Because Leontuzzo is not here as a witness to tell you about his father or opine about his actions.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: The case being heard today concerns the ownership of the new city.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Leontuzzo arbitrarily determined what is to come in this new city, and in Siracusa as a whole.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Leontuzzo, please explain to us why Signora Sicilia chose you.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I was both my father's accomplice in everything that happened, as well as the one who stopped him.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I became the latter after I learned the truth.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I believe that my father was misguided, and that his actions would not bring a new era to Siracusa.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Even if dragging all the famiglie into a war would somehow see them erase each other in the end, it does not necessarily mean that the people would choose a new way of life.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: But beyond that, I saw a real opportunity in all this.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: So, at the end of everything, I went to Signora Sicilia and asked to borrow a city from Siracusa.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: 'A city without famiglie.'

steps.name: Irascible Famiglia Juror
steps.text: Another joke? Why would Signora Sicilia ever agree to that?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Because it wasn't actually a request. It was a challenge to Siracusa.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: In Signora Sicilia's eyes, my father's methods violated her order, and she couldn't tolerate that.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: But the method I chose... Though I don't want to put it this way, was something she found permissible. Otherwise, I wouldn't even be standing here speaking to all of you.
Leontuzzo looks in a certain direction, to where a Sankta priest is standing.
The blindfolded priest does not seem to be paying attention to the ongoing trial.

steps.name: Keen Famiglia Juror
steps.text: Alright. If what you say is true, then Signora Sicilia's order does make more sense...

steps.name: Keen Famiglia Juror
steps.text: Or I guess, this is the only explanation for why Signora Sicilia would've decided that.

steps.name: Composed Famiglia Juror
steps.text: If this really is true, Leontuzzo, then everything you're doing today is just for show.

steps.name: Composed Famiglia Juror
steps.text: Call this a trial? You might be standing here, this is all just announcing you as owner of the new city. Isn't that right?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: No, this city does not belong to me.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: The new city will have everything you'd expect it to, with one exception—famiglie.

steps.name: Composed Famiglia Juror
steps.text: You really think you can keep them out?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: What a stupid question. It's just as if I asked you, has the boundary between famiglie and ordinary civilians ever been respected?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Famiglie are only willing to abide by Signora Sicilia's rules because she's strong enough to dominate them.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: And this gentleman's agreement among famiglie only exists because they don't have what it takes to wipe each other out.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Of course you'll come to the city. I know that, obviously.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: But this time, you'll see what it is you've always underestimated.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Of course, I will welcome any famiglie looking to bring change as partners in the new city.

steps.name: Calm Civilian Juror
steps.text: I don't think there's any difference between 'a city without famiglie' and 'Siracusa without famiglie.' They're both crazy.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Do you say that because it's unrealistic, or because it's hard?

steps.name: Calm Civilian Juror
steps.text: Because it's unrealistic, of course.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: My father was definitely misguided, but I don't think either of these ideas are unrealistic.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: You're just too used to letting your eyes decide what is and is not realistic.

steps.name: Calm Civilian Juror
steps.text: The famiglia are deeply ingrained into this land. You can't hope to uproot them. Nobody can.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: But famiglie can be changed, and they can become more civilized.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Even if they can't be wiped out, they should be changed into something else. And as long as that something else is what we want, then that's fine too.

steps.name: Calm Civilian Juror
steps.text: And you really think you can make that work?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I might fail, but don't you think it's worth a shot?

steps.name: Serious Government Observer
steps.text: The only thing you've won for yourself is a handout from Signora Sicilia.

steps.name: Serious Government Observer
steps.text: The famiglia system still exists. Though it may appear shaky right now, it is by no means so easy to topple.

steps.name: Serious Government Observer
steps.text: No matter if this business today is serious or just for show, it's only possible because you have Signora Sicilia's permission.

steps.name: Serious Government Observer
steps.text: Is there actually any point to all of this?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Unfortunately, if things don't pan out the way I want them to, then I'm afraid we'll simply be replaced like a tablecloth.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Plus, I've never considered my success inevitable. That day, I was honestly ready to die.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: But that doesn't mean I won't take an opportunity that presents itself, handout or not.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Maybe in some other place, given the same set of circumstances, someone in my position could've been a better person and turned down the handout.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: But in Siracusa, at this very moment, if this is the only way to move things forward, then that is the pill I will swallow.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Would Ministro Rubio have done what he did, if there was another option?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Are you aware of the consequences?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: What we're doing is unprecedented. How am I supposed to guess what the consequences will be?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: But, this is what I believe.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Lavinia, I owe an answer not only to all of Volsinii, but to you and everyone around you. Right?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: After that day, we didn't get a chance to talk things through, and only had a vague idea of what the other was thinking.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Are we really walking down the same path?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Is the new city that I want the same as the one you want?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: We don't really know how the other thinks, do we?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: ...I trust you.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: If you trust me, that's all the more reason to pass judgment on me.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Not just for your sake, but for all the officials who've rallied around you because of Rubio.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Otherwise, what reason would they have to trust me, a man who was mafia royalty?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: This isn't a burden you have to carry alone.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I ought to shoulder the responsibility with you.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: No... I've finally come to understand the words you said to me, Lavinia.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Our world views are fundamentally different.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: As the former heir to a famiglia, there's no way I can empathize with your perspectives and experiences.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: What I have to suffer now... is just dealing with whatever's left over after unloading that identity.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Also, from a utilitarian perspective, the people trust you, and this is a real chance for you to lock in that image.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: If you put it like that, I'm afraid a lot of people will see this trial as nothing more than a show.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Let them think that then. It doesn't matter.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Even if they do think it's a show, sometimes, the willingness to put on a show is already a gesture in its own right. Don't you think?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Anyway, Lavinia, that's what I think.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: We haven't accomplished anything big just yet.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: One day, we'll end up mistrusting each other.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: One day, when we come to our senses, we might realize that we've been misguided all along.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Leontuzzo Bellone, what is it that makes you stand here so resolutely?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: You were born into a famiglia, yet now, you've become the famiglie's worst enemy. Why?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Why, huh... I ask myself the same question a lot.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Is it my idea of chasing efficiency?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Was I raised on ideals of justice?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Is it because of the actions of an admirable government official?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Is it a conclusion from a minor observation of changes in the famiglie?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Maybe all of the above.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: If we put all these reasons together, we might be able to come up with an answer––

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: The time has come.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Maybe Carracci avoided assassination and became a successful Ministero dei Lavori Pubblici, working hard towards a similar goal.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Maybe Ministro Rubio chose to show restraint and continued to occupy his position, secretly winning people over with his lofty ideals and striving to bring change to Siracusa.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: This wasn't some elaborate plan I've been hatching my whole life. It suddenly dawned on me at some point, and I only made it this far on luck.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: If I die, there'll be someone who comes after me, and another man after that.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: And none of this is a testament to how hard I work or how unique I am. It just means that––

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: The time has come for Siracusa to change.
One question after another is thrown at Leontuzzo, the entire court filled with voices interrogative and vitriolic.
He stands in the center of the courtroom, earnestly and tirelessly answering every question he deems worthwhile.
Slowly but surely, more and more people begin to think that this young man is actually quite thoughtful, and that––
He's serious.
In the end, the courtroom's entire atmosphere seems to cower before him.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: All the jurors present, all the civilians watching, and all the people tuning in through various media.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Until now, my heart has been filled with uneasiness.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I borrowed this city from Signora Sicilia, but never saw it as something that belonged to me.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I borrowed this city from Signora Sicilia so we could work together to build something completely new, for all of you to work towards a Siracusa free from the famiglie.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Because I made that decision on everyone's behalf, I must also face everyone's judgment.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: But, if you'll let me make a single grand statement–

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: At this moment, Siracusa doesn't have the right to judge me.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: And so, I can only be judged... by all of you.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: You will receive this right, just as if you had won the power to build an entirely new city.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Maybe one day, at one point in the future, the power to determine Siracusa's future will also lie in your hands.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: This new city welcomes all of those dissatisfied living under the yoke of the famiglie and those who have their doubts, including doubts about me.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: That's all I wanted to say.

a.text: The trial, believed to be Leontuzzo's first public speech as Nuovo Volsinii's mayoral candidate, sparked widespread discussion as well as heated resistance from some famiglie.
But without a doubt, this one-man show of a trial at long last laid the foundations for Nuovo Volsinii to truly come into fruition.
It is but a new beginning.
